target_customer: Small-batch wineries in the US that need inventory tracking and point of sale
problem: Small wineries track bottles, cases and tasting room sales across disconnected tools. CraftOS offered one inventory and POS system built for wine.
product_category: Vertical inventory management and POS software for wineries

founders.name: Wael Al Sallami
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led development of Square Online at Weebly and Square. The YC page lists him as the only founder; a separate YC launch for Martola credits Wael and a Kenan with no last name.

technical_complexity.rationale: Inventory tracking plus POS is standard CRUD and payments integration; the hard parts are alcohol compliance reporting and hardware, which no source says CraftOS built.

defensibility.rationale: Inventory and POS data create some switching cost once a winery runs on it, but winery software vendors already existed and a three person team had little else to defend with.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes incumbents acting against CraftOS. The founder later launched Martola, a different product, per the YC page.

market_need_then: The YC page states that small-batch wineries produce 83% of US wine, which frames a large count of small buyers, but no source gives customer counts, revenue or evidence of spend.

branding.domain_note: Used craftos.com, which no longer resolves from this session; the history of how it was acquired is not found.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found no press, community or brand pages for CraftOS, so the brand left no visible trace.

outcome_analysis: The cause of CraftOS ending is not public. The YC page marks it Inactive and shows the founder launching Martola, an invoice matching product for retailers, so the founder appears to have moved to a different idea. The search found no shutdown post, no customer figures and only a single database figure of 500 thousand dollars of pre-seed, so no failure factor can be assigned from evidence.
notes: craftos.com did not resolve (DNS failure), so the site status is unknown. The 500K pre-seed rests on VCBacked and similar aggregators; one directory shows no funding and another lists a convertible note. Latest-search results gave only 2026 competitor snapshots, so the competitor list is empty. The loot-drop description of CraftOS as a general retail platform conflicts with the YC description and is ignored.
